subject: ela
intro: Analyze structural choices and their effects.

items.prompt:
A hint about events to come is called:
A) foreshadowing
B) a flashback
C) a glossary

A scene that jumps back to the past is a:
A) flashback
B) climax
C) stanza

The speed at which events unfold is the story's:
A) pacing
B) title
C) margin

An author plants an early detail that only becomes meaningful at the end. This technique:
A) is foreshadowing, building anticipation and a payoff
B) is a flashback
C) has no effect
items.answer: A) is foreshadowing, building anticipation and a payoff

steps: Early hint = foreshadowing. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) is foreshadowing, building anticipation and a payoff

items.prompt:
Why might an author alternate between two timelines (a crime and its later investigation)?
A) to build suspense about how they connect
B) to confuse for no reason
C) to end sooner
items.answer: A) to build suspense about how they connect

steps: Dual timeline builds tension. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) to build suspense about how they connect

items.prompt:
Ending a chapter mid-action mainly:
A) creates suspense
B) resolves the plot
C) removes tension

steps: Leaves reader hanging. Key is A.

items.prompt:
A thriller reveals the villain's identity to the reader early but keeps the hero in the dark. This structural choice creates:
A) dramatic irony and suspense
B) a flashback
C) no effect

steps: Reader knows more. Key is A.

items.prompt:
An author uses foreshadowing in chapter one that pays off in the finale. The MOST likely purpose is to:
A) build anticipation and make the ending feel earned
B) pad the length
C) hide the plot
items.answer: A) build anticipation and make the ending feel earned

steps: Foreshadowing sets up payoff. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) build anticipation and make the ending feel earned
